channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: NVIDIA and Sapphire join Reactor’s Series A: the bet that world models need real-time infrastructure
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reactor announced Monday that NVIDIA and Sapphire Ventures have joined its Lightspeed-led Series A, as demand grows for infrastructure that can run generative video and world models in real time — at 60+ FPS and sub-40ms latency.

item.title: OpenAI turns ChatGPT's image-loading screen into ad space: visual ads start testing this month
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI announced Monday that it will test a visual ad format inside ChatGPT's image generation later this month in the US, alongside expanded measurement tools and brand-safety pilots with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science.

item.title: Altman tells Politico the world should “accept some bad things” from AI — his split with Anthropic goes public
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: In a Politico Decoded interview released Monday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the world should “accept some bad things happening” from AI in exchange for broad access, drew his line at “a serious loss of control to AI,” and put distance between OpenAI and Anthropic on regulation — drawing swift fire from critics.

item.title: GIGABYTE takes local AI to Abu Dhabi: 1-PFLOPS desktop box, 20-PFLOPS GB300 workstation
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: GIGABYTE’s Ai Everything Abu Dhabi showcase pairs the 1-PFLOPS AI TOP ATOM personal supercomputer — now with four-node clustering and 512GB of aggregate memory — with the W775-V10 desk-side workstation on NVIDIA’s GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra at 20 PFLOPS. The pitch: develop and fine-tune locally, scale to the cloud later.

item.title: The FBI's new deepfake hunter: Cyabra wins a seat on the Bureau's five-year AI detection contract
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cyabra announced Monday it won positions on the FBI's Specialized OSINT Tools contract, putting its AI deepfake-detection platform on the Bureau's approved list for image and video analysis through 2031.

item.title: Reflection unveils Beam: a 501B open-weight model built to match China's best at 3–4x less compute
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reflection AI introduced Beam, its first frontier open-weight model — a 501B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 23B active parameters, trained on 23.8 trillion tokens — claiming parity with China's leading open models at a fraction of the inference cost.

item.title: Valon raises $150M at a $2.3B valuation to put AI agents to work on one in six U.S. mortgages
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Valon Technologies announced a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation — double its last mark — with Ribbit Capital joining and Andreessen Horowitz participating. The money accelerates ValonOS, its AI-native servicing platform, already under contract on one in six outstanding U.S. mortgages, with AI agents answering homeowner emails, allocating payments, and running escrow analyses.

item.title: Run Claude Code on DeepSeek: route every coding agent through one local gateway
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Magpie (yetone/magpie, 5,100+ stars, MIT) is a local model gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425 that runs Claude Code on DeepSeek, Codex on Kimi, or Gemini CLI on GLM - with routing groups that fail over when a quota runs dry. Setup, routing, and honest limits, hands-on.

item.title: Claude comes home to India: Anthropic switches on in-country inference via Amazon Bedrock
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic has switched on in-country Claude inference in India through Amazon Bedrock, so requests via the India endpoint are processed on Indian servers — unlocking Claude for banks, insurers, and government workloads that demand data residency.

item.title: Teradyne bets on the AI factory floor — strategic investment in Bright Machines fuses robots, test tech, and software-defined microfactories
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Teradyne announced an undisclosed strategic investment in Bright Machines plus a collaboration to fuse robotic assembly, board test, and software-defined manufacturing for AI infrastructure — chasing one end-to-end production data thread, from design to electrical test.

item.title: XTEND patents drones that take orders from their payloads — XOS lets smart payloads steer missions in real time
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: XTEND AI Robotics announced on October 5 that the USPTO granted U.S. Utility Patent No. 12,743,960, covering a system where a smart payload feeds real-time navigation instructions to the drone carrying it through XOS — so the platform adapts to what's on board while the operator stays in command.

item.title: Shift Bioscience recalibrates AI virtual cells: Nature Biotechnology paper says the benchmarks were broken
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Shift Bioscience announced on October 5 that new research in Nature Biotechnology shows genetic perturbation models underperform partly because benchmark metrics are miscalibrated — and it will use the fixed yardstick to hunt rejuvenation and age-related disease targets.

item.title: Agentic Checkout: Constructor embeds Stripe in its AI shopping agents — buy inside the conversation
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Constructor announced Agentic Checkout on October 5: Stripe — including Link — now works inside its onsite AI shopping agents, so shoppers can discover products, ask questions, and pay without leaving the conversation.

item.title: Safeworld exits stealth with a $12M+ seed to stress-test gen-AI robots in simulation
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Safeworld emerged from stealth on October 5 with a $12M+ seed led by Shine Capital and a16z Speedrun: CMU Safe AI lab director Ding Zhao wants to be the independent safety referee for generative-AI robots.

item.title: Stop refreshing job boards: build your own AI job hunter with JobRadar
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: JobRadar (suvamneog/jobradar, 150+ stars, MIT) watches 56 companies' job boards across seven ATS platforms, scores every posting 0–10 against your resume with an LLM, and emails the matches. Setup, scoring rules, and honest limits, hands-on.

item.title: Physitrack prices its AI-powered EMR at $59.99 a month, $19 for the AI scribe — 100 clinics sign up in five days
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Physitrack revealed the commercial model for its AI-powered electronic medical record for physical therapy: free through early access until January 2027, then $59.99 per user per month — with a $19 AI scribe add-on. More than 100 clinics signed up in the first five days.

item.title: OneByZero raises $20M Series A: Jungle Ventures bets on AI engineers who live inside the client
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Singapore's OneByZero raised a $20 million Series A led by Jungle Ventures — its first external funding — to scale its forward-deployed model of embedding engineers inside banks and telecoms to run governed AI agents on its NEO platform.

item.title: Nvidia and Blackstone take half of Firmus’s A$5.5B IPO: insiders top up as demand swamps the float
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Bloomberg reports that roughly half of Firmus Grid’s record Australian IPO will go to existing holders, letting Nvidia and Blackstone increase their stakes at A$11 a share.

item.title: OpenAI’s Codex chief sets a 28-day clock: ship a daily improvement or reset everyone’s usage
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux pledged that every day for the next 28 days, Codex and ChatGPT Work will either ship a clear improvement for most users — or undergo a full usage reset. The team narrows to four areas: a simpler product, more usable capacity, breakthrough features, and new models.

item.title: Stop nursing broken selectors: describe your tests in plain English — hands-on with e2e
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: e2e (tester-army/e2e, 3,400+ stars, Apache-2.0) is an end-to-end testing framework where an AI agent drives your web or mobile app from natural-language goals, while deterministic locators and assertions keep the verdict honest. Here’s npx e2e init, the agent.act/agent.assert API, the zero-model-call replay trick, and the honest limits.

item.title: Huawei and Qualcomm sign their first 5G patent deal — with an AI cross-license attached
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Huawei and Qualcomm signed a broad multiyear patent license agreement covering 5G, compute, AI and networking — the first 5G patent deal between the two, and the first time Huawei has licensed or assigned AI and compute patents to the U.S. chip designer.

item.title: Hark launches this week: Brett Adcock promises the first 100,000 users a free paid plan
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Brett Adcock says Hark, the $700M-backed personal-AI lab he seeded with $100M of his own money, launches its first product this week — and the first 100,000 registered users get the paid plan free.

item.title: SCM brings local AI search to every photo — and every video frame — on your Mac
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SCM (Screen Memories) is an open-source macOS app that indexes any folder of photos and videos entirely on-device — CLIP/SigLIP vision search, Tesseract OCR in 36+ languages, Whisper transcripts, and an opt-in local LLM. It hit Hacker News today.

item.title: Anthropic whistleblower Jacob Coxon will testify at NYC's AI hearing Monday — Bloomberg
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Bloomberg reported Sunday that Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic researcher who quit last month warning AI labs are 'gambling with our lives,' will testify Monday at a New York City Council AI hearing — at Speaker Julie Menin's request, as lawmakers weigh a package of safety bills.

item.title: Run a 125-billion-parameter model on your own gaming PC: hands-on with Strata
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Strata (Niko1221/Strata, 11,000+ stars in ten days, MIT) runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — a 125-billion-parameter model — on a gaming PC with 12 GB of VRAM and 32 GB of RAM. One-click install, an OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:8080, and about 53 tokens per second on an RTX 5070. Here’s the hardware check, the model sizes, and how to point your coding agents at it.
